faq: How many variants can my store handle?
Platforms set their own limits on options and variants. We check yours first and suggest a simpler structure if a product has too many combinations, for example by splitting one product into two.
Can you set up bundles that discount automatically?
We can set up bundle products and, where your platform supports it, a simple discount rule. Advanced bundle logic may need a paid app, billed by the app maker. We tell you before we install anything.
Will changing variants affect my past orders?
Past orders keep the details they were placed with. For live products we avoid deleting variants that have sales, and edit them instead. We also back up the product data in a sheet first.
Can you merge separate listings into one product?
Yes. We combine listings such as a shirt sold as five separate products into one product with options, keep the best images and set redirects from the old pages. You approve the merge plan first.
desc:
Product variants and options setup lets shoppers choose sizes, colors and bundles without confusion, while price, SKU and stock stay accurate for each choice. Ecom Swift LLC builds the option structure, matches images to variants and tests the selector on a phone and a computer.

## What are product variants and options?

An option is a choice a shopper makes, such as size, color or material. A variant is one specific combination of those choices, for example a medium shirt in navy. Each variant can carry its own price, SKU, barcode, stock count, weight and image.

Setting these up properly means a shopper sees only valid choices, the right photo appears when they pick a color and the store tracks stock for every combination. Setting them up poorly leads to oversell, wrong shipments and abandoned carts.

## Why option setup trips up shoppers

A selector that lists "Red / Small / Cotton / Standard" in one confusing dropdown makes people guess. Another common fault is a color option that changes no photo, so the buyer cannot tell what they are choosing. Sold-out sizes shown as normal buttons waste a click and cause frustration.

On the owner's side, messy variants cause real trouble in the stockroom. If two listings sell the same item as separate products, stock counts drift apart. If option names differ across the store, filters show "XL", "Extra Large" and "X-Large" as three separate choices.

## How options affect orders and returns

Clear options turn browsing into a confident purchase. When each choice is labeled in plain words, the photo changes with the color and unavailable choices are marked, shoppers complete the selection quickly. Clear sizing information, such as a size guide, reduces wrong-size orders, which in turn lowers returns and exchange handling.

Bundles and add-ons can raise the value of an order without extra effort from you. A set of related products offered as one choice, or a gift option on a single product, gives shoppers a simple way to buy more. Where a bundle uses a special discount, a third-party app may be needed, and we will tell you before we set one up.

## What a good variant setup includes

- Option names in a clear order, such as color first and then size.
- One standard naming style for every product across the store.
- A separate price, SKU and stock count for each variant that needs one.
- Barcodes entered where your products have them.
- A photo matched to each color or style.
- Sold-out options labeled properly rather than hidden or left misleading.
- A size guide table on products that need one.
- Bundles or sets built for items that sell together.
- Gift and add-on options, where your store supports them.
- A phone and desktop test of the full selection path.

## How we build it

We start by listing every product with variants and how its options are currently arranged. Then we agree on an option order and naming style with you, and we apply it product by product.

The Basic package covers a small group of products with clean sizes and colors. Standard widens the scope with variant images, a size guide and up to three option types per product. Premium covers a larger group, a number of bundles or sets, gift and add-on options, store-wide standard option names and a short guide for adding variants later. Each store platform has its own limits on how many options and variants a product can hold, so we plan around those limits and explain any trade-offs.

If you have separate listings that really are one product, we can merge them, taking care to keep order history and links intact.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Put the choice that changes the photo, usually color, first.
- Use the same size labels everywhere.
- Keep each SKU unique and meaningful.
- Test every product type on a phone before launch.

**Avoid:**
- Hiding variant stock in product notes.
- Creating a separate product for each size.
- Using vague labels such as "Option 1".
- Offering far more choices than a shopper can sensibly compare.

## Who this service is for

It suits an apparel or accessories shop with many sizes and colors that is struggling with stock errors. It suits a seller launching gift sets who wants a simple way to offer them. It also suits a store owner who has inherited a catalog with inconsistent option names and wants a clean standard.

## What we need and how to begin

Send us the list of products with their sizes, colors and prices, plus the photo for each color if you have it. Give us a collaborator or staff login created from your own account, never your password. If you want bundles, tell us which products belong together and how you want them priced.
